texts.li: [orphaned,!baby] {A_nameDef} has no parent left here to raise {A_objective}. {B_nameDef} has been looking in on {A_objective}, and the colony asks the council who should raise {A_nameDef} now.

[orphaned,!baby] {A_nameDef} keeps asking who {A_pronoun} belongs to now. {B_nameDef} would take {A_objective} in if the council agrees, though some say {A_nameDef} should choose for {A_objective}self.
[orphaned,baby] {A_nameDef} is too small to know {A_pronoun} has lost anyone. Somebody has to raise {A_objective}, and {B_nameDef} has offered.

[!orphaned,!baby] {A_nameDef} has nobody of {A_possessive} own here: no parent at the table, nobody to run to. {B_nameDef} has been keeping an eye on {A_objective}, and asks the council whether {B_pronoun} should raise {A_objective} as {B_possessive} own.
[!orphaned,!baby] Everyone feeds {A_nameDef} and nobody tucks {A_objective} in. {B_nameDef} has asked the council to settle whose {A_pronoun} is.
[!orphaned,baby] {A_nameDef} has nobody of {A_possessive} own. Whoever is nearest feeds {A_objective}, and {B_nameDef} would like it to be {B_objective}, always.

li.label: {B_nameDef} raises {A_nameDef} as {B_possessive} own
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} is raising {A_nameDef} as {B_possessive} own now. That first evening {B_pronoun} kept {A_objective} company a long while, and didn't hurry away.

outcomes.li: [!baby] {B_nameDef} is raising {A_nameDef} as {B_possessive} own now. They spent the first evening together, and {A_nameDef} asked whether it was for good. {B_nameDef} said it was.
[baby] {B_nameDef} is raising {A_nameDef} as {B_possessive} own now. The first evening {B_pronoun} stayed by {A_objective} a long while, saying nothing much, which {A_nameDef} seemed to like.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} choose
li.outcome: Asked who {A_pronoun} wanted, {A_nameDef} went to {B_nameDef} and stayed with {B_objective}. {B_nameDef} is raising {A_objective} now.

outcomes.li: [orphaned] Asked who {A_pronoun} wanted, {A_nameDef} went to {B_nameDef} without a word and stayed there. {B_nameDef} is raising {A_objective} now, and was more pleased than {B_pronoun} let on.

li.label: The whole colony raises {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: At supper the council said it plainly: {A_nameDef} belongs to all of them, and anyone at the table can be asked. {A_nameDef} has a great many grown-ups now, and none of them {A_possessive} own.

texts.li: [engaged] {A_nameDef} {LASTA} and {B_nameDef} {LASTB} are to be married, and mean to keep their own names. Some say a family should go by one, and the two have asked the council what it thinks.

[engaged] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} are engaged, and the talk at supper is whose name they will go by. {A_nameDef} has said {A_pronoun} would gladly be a {LASTB}, and asked the council to settle it.
[engaged] There will be a wedding soon, and one question left over: will it be {LASTA} and {LASTB} still, or one name for the two of them? {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} would like the council to say.
[!engaged] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} have been married a while and still go by two names. {A_nameDef} has wondered aloud about taking the {LASTB} name, and asked the council to settle it.
[!engaged] Married, and still {LASTA} and {LASTB}: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} have asked the council whether one of them should take the other's name.
{A_nameDef} {LASTA} and {B_nameDef} {LASTB} have put a small question to the council: should they go by one family name?

li.label: {A_nameDef} takes the {LASTB} name
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} goes by {LASTB} now, the same as {B_nameDef}, and the colony is still getting used to it.

outcomes.li: [engaged] When they marry, {A_nameDef} will take the {LASTB} name. {B_nameDef} tried not to look pleased about it, and failed.
[!engaged] {A_nameDef} goes by {LASTB} now, the same as {B_nameDef}. The council wrote it into the colony's chronicle, and that was that.

li.label: {B_nameDef} takes the {LASTA} name
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} goes by {LASTA} now, the same as {A_nameDef}, and the colony is still getting used to it.

outcomes.li: [engaged] When they marry, {B_nameDef} will take the {LASTA} name. {A_nameDef} hadn't expected it, and was more pleased than {A_pronoun} let on.

li.label: Each keeps their own name
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} {LASTA} and {B_nameDef} {LASTB} keep their own names. The council said a family is the people in it, not what they are called.

outcomes.li: [engaged] They will marry as {A_nameDef} {LASTA} and {B_nameDef} {LASTB}, each with their own name. The council said a family is the people in it, not what they are called.
